discussion_comments.comment_body:
Thanks — we considered this and are intentionally leaving it as-is.

`NPM_ARGS` here deliberately mirrors the CLI installer (`tools/installer/modules/custom-module-manager.js:551`), which has run `npm install` **without** `--ignore-scripts` since #2229 — well before this branch. So this isn't a regression introduced here; it's the established project-wide default for community-module installs, which are already an explicit trust decision (a module's skills/agents/scripts run when you use it).

Adding `--ignore-scripts` to only the skill path would make it stricter than the installer and create an inconsistency, while leaving the more-common CLI path just as exposed. If we want this hardening it should be a deliberate policy applied to **both** the skill and the installer (ideally behind an opt-in), tracked as its own change — not slipped into this PR. Leaving as-is.

Fixed in 02806ba4 — using the existing `safePathInsideRoot` helper (rejects `..`/absolute/symlink escapes) rather than a new resolve. A traversal subdir now throws `EXIT.PATH_TRAVERSAL` before any copy out of the shared clone cache.

Fixed in 02806ba4 as defense-in-depth, reusing `safePathInsideRoot` (instead of a new `resolveInside`): the module root and `--purge` custom dir are containment-checked (throw `PATH_TRAVERSAL` on escape), and each files-manifest path is validated before `fs.rm` — skipped with a warning if it escapes `_bmad/`.

Fixed in 02806ba4 — same approach as remove: the swap `targetDir` is containment-checked before `atomicSwapDir` (throws `PATH_TRAVERSAL` on escape) and each manifest path in the modified-file scan is validated via `safePathInsideRoot`.
